title: Curio Labs - Hosted Embeddings + Rerank Demo
summary: AE+SE walked Curio through Redwood hosted embeddings + reranking endpoints. Covered architecture for vector store + Redwood reranker, tradeoffs (latency vs cost), caching and batching knobs, security (SOC2, KMS, VPC), and pilot next steps. Customer wants a 4-week pilot to validate recall@k and end-to-end latency under traffic.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, joining with Diego from SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:18] Jordan (Curio): Good, thanks. Excited to see how you handle embeddings + rerank, we then want to replace our current vector pipeline.
[00:28] Diego (SE): Awesome. Quick agenda: we'll do a short intro, demo the hosted embeddings endpoint, show a basic retrieval + Redwood reranker flow, then discuss perf and security.
[00:48] Priya (CTO): Quick ask up front: data residency concerns — we need EU region and SOC2 documentation.
[00:58] Maya: Yep, we'll cover that. We also have a private deployment option but first the hosted flow.
[01:15] Liam (Data Eng): Also curious about indexing — do you expect us to use FAISS, Pinecone, or can Redwood do the whole rerank?
[01:35] Diego: Good Q. You can keep whatever vector store you like, Redwood's reranker consumes embeddings and a candidate set. For hosted customers many use managed stores (Pinecone) or self-hosted FAISS. We also provide embeddings via API so you can compute and store vectors yourself.
[02:02] Jordan: Walk us through the API calls, like sample payloads and latencies.
[02:14] Diego: Sure, I'll share screen, quick curl example: POST /v1/embeddings with text, dimension 1536 model_cpu." [note: screen demo audio in background] "[02:38] Diego: For rerank we have a single endpoint /v1/rerank that takes query, candidate_ids, and optionally raw candidate texts. We support both dense dot-product scoring and an NN-cache optimized reranker that runs a small transformer on the top-100 candidates.
[03:10] Jordan: Top-100, ok. What latency should we expect for a 3-token query and 100 candidates?
[03:25] Diego: On our hosted tier typical median is 85-120ms for rerank at top-100 for xlarge models, and down to 30-60ms for the smaller rerank-lite variants. End-to-end with an external vector store lookup add another ~10-40ms depending on the store.
[03:52] Priya: What about cost? If we do 1M queries per month at top-100 rerank, what's the rough bill?
[04:05] Maya: We'll send exact pricing, but rough rule: embeddings generation cost per 1M vectors and rerank cost per 1M candidates scored. It depends on model family and batching. Our Optimize product can suggest batching to reduce unit cost.
[04:30] Jordan: Can you show the Console for tuning?
[04:36] Diego: Yeah, flapping over to Console — here you can see per-route latency, token-level cost, and our recommended batch sizes. On the left we show the rerank route with historical R@10 and mean reciprocal rank.
[05:05] Maya: The Console also surfaces prompt sets you upload and tracks regressions. So you can pin a model version and roll back if relevance drops.
[05:24] Liam: When you say 'pin model', is that just a config or do you host multiple model variants?
[05:33] Diego: It's both. Config layer lets you set a model alias to a specific version. Under the hood we can route to quantized variants or smaller models for cost savings.
[05:50] Jordan: Do you do prefix/KV caching for chat-like contexts? We have a lot of repeated queries with similar prefixes.
[05:59] Diego: For generation we do KV caching; for rerank specifically we have candidate caching and a prefix-level caching for common queries which dramatically reduces per-request compute.
[06:18] Priya: Security — KMS integration and audit logs?
[06:25] Maya: Hosted supports customer-managed KMS, full audit logs in the Console, and SOC2 plus ISO options. For VPC peering or Private deployment that's also available. We'll send the compliance pack.
[06:41] Jordan: Cool. Can you run a quick example with our sample docs? We shared a small dataset earlier.
[06:48] Diego: Yes let's try. I'll call embeddings on a sample doc, then run a basic retrieval with the reranker.
[07:05] [screen demo noise, brief pause]
[07:30] Diego: Ok output: embedding vector looks good, cosine similarity returns 12 candidate ids. Feeding top-50 into the reranker now.
[07:48] Jordan: I see the score distribution, some candidates jumped to top-3 after rerank, that's promising.
[08:04] Diego: Note the reranker model reorders based on context and is tuned for precision at top-K.
[08:20] Priya: If we wanted to self-host the reranker model later, is that possible?
[08:28] Diego: Yep, with Redwood Private you'll get a customer-managed control plane and can run on your infra. The same API semantics apply so code changes minimal.
[08:42] Liam: A practical question: our pipeline currently uses 768-d embeddings, do you recommend migrating to 1536?
[08:53] Diego: 1536 tends to give better separation for reranking, but Optimize can run a quick eval with your dataset and recommend. Often we see diminishing returns after 1024-1536 depending on corpus.
[09:12] Jordan: Can you explain quantization tradeoffs for the reranker?
[09:18] Diego: Sure — we recommend int8 or q4 variants for candidate scoring when latency is critical. For the heavy reranker transformers we often use q4_0 to preserve quality while reducing memory and improving throughput. We'll provide empirical numbers from similar customers.
[09:44] Priya: How do you measure recall and relevance in the Console? We need to report R@1 R@5 R@10 and MRR to execs.
[09:53] Maya: Console tracks R@K on uploaded labeled sets and ties regressions to deploys. You can upload ground-truth pairs and Console will compute those metrics over time.
[10:10] Jordan: Anything on cold-start for new docs? Our dataset is frequently updated.
[10:17] Diego: For frequent updates we recommend incremental embedding writes and warm-up queries. Our autoscaling handles load but write-heavy ingestion needs tuning on batch sizes.
[10:35] Jordan: Can you explain the fallback policies? If the large model is overloaded, do you auto-fallback to a smaller reranker?
[10:42] Diego: Yes, smart routing lets you set fallbacks by policy: latency-first route to smaller model, cost-first to a quantized model, or region-first. Fallbacks keep service online albeit with different quality.
[11:02] Priya: Audit and logging specifics — retention and export options?
[11:09] Maya: Logs can be exported to your S3 or BigQuery with customer-controlled retention. We also support log forwarding to SIEMs.
[11:22] Liam: Any particular gotchas with vector stores? We saw issues with recall when using approximate NN with low ef/search_k.
[11:30] Diego: Right — index config matters. We recommend tuning ef/search_k and using a candidate expansion to compensate for ANN misses before rerank.
[11:47] Jordan: Can we run a small benchmark — synthetic 10k queries to measure p50/p95 latency and R@10?
[11:55] Maya: Yes, we typically do a 2-week pilot with a scoped benchmark. For this call we can schedule a 10k-run with your sample.
[12:05] [longer demo segment — screen sharing, typing sounds]
[15:10] Diego: One thing to watch: batching. If you batch embeddings requests you improve throughput but increase per-request latency. Console shows per-route batching recommendations.
[16:00] Jordan: How do you handle versioning of embedding models? We'll need stable vectors for offline indexes.
[16:08] Diego: You can pin a model for inference; when migrating models Console can run shadow evaluations. For index migration we recommend reindexing or using dual indexes during a rollout.
[16:34] Priya: SLA questions — what's the uptime SLO for hosted rerank endpoints?
[16:41] Maya: Hosted standard has 99.9% for API endpoints; dedicated has higher SLOs with contractual terms.
[16:50] Jordan: Any notes on data retention for embeddings? We need to keep vectors for 12 months but with strict deletion controls.
[16:59] Maya: We support retention policies and can configure auto-delete windows. We'll detail that in the security pack.
[17:12] Liam: Ok can you show the Optimize recommendations for our workload?
[17:19] Diego: Pulling the Optimize tab — here it analyzed token distribution and suggested smaller reranker for queries under 6 tokens and use of a candidate-cache with TTL 24h for repeat queries, saving ~30% cost in similar customers.
[17:45] Jordan: Interesting. Do you have actual before/after numbers?
[17:51] Diego: We'll share a benchmarking sheet; quick example from a media customer: 40% cost reduction with a combined cache+batching strategy while keeping R@10 within 1% of baseline.
[18:12] Priya: Onboarding timeline if we do a pilot?
[18:18] Maya: Typical pilot is 2-4 weeks. First week: access + baseline ingestion. Week 2: run benchmark and tune. Week 3-4: iterate and produce a recommendation report.
[18:30] Jordan: What do you need from us to start?
[18:34] Maya: 1) sample dataset and ground-truth query pairs, 2) expected throughput, 3) security contact for SOC2 questions.
[18:46] Jordan: We'll share that by Monday.
[18:52] Diego: Great. One more note: when you run rerank at scale, watch tokenization differences across models; we normalize for that in our eval toolkit.
[19:05] [short pause]
[19:28] Priya: Any integration examples for node/java/python?
[19:33] Diego: We have SDKs in Python and Node and examples in our docs repo. I'll drop links.
[19:46] Liam: Do you allow persisted caches or is cache ephemeral?
[19:52] Diego: Candidate caches can be persisted with TTL and backed by Redis or in our managed store depending on architecture.
[20:10] Jordan: Are there limitations on candidate size transmitted to rerank endpoint? We worry about network payloads.
[20:19] Diego: We recommend sending top-100 candidate ids and only include text for top-20 if you want context; that keeps payloads small.
[20:36] Priya: Ok we've got cost concerns; for budgeting, would you help produce a cost estimate?
[20:43] Maya: Yes we'll produce a tailored estimate based on your RPS and candidate sizes.
[21:00] [demo wrap-up noises]
[21:18] Jordan: Quick question on A/B testing — we want to try several reranker models in production.
[21:26] Diego: Console supports canary and A/B with automatic metrics comparison and rollback. You can route percentage traffic to different model variants.
[21:45] Priya: Any specific compliance for EU data residency?
[21:52] Maya: We have EU hosting regions and can sign data processing addenda.
[22:07] Jordan: Can you explain telemetry sampling? We don't want to log full PII.
[22:14] Diego: We sample at route level and redact PII by default; telemetry you can configure to mask or drop fields.
[22:34] [long pause, typing]
[23:10] Maya: Let's recap next steps and owners.
[23:16] Jordan: Sounds good.
[23:22] Diego: Recap: we'll send security and pricing docs, set up a pilot account, and schedule the 10k benchmark run.
[23:34] Priya: I want a list of expected artifacts for the pilot.
[23:40] Maya: We'll send a pilot checklist: data format, auth, sample queries, success metrics.
[23:50] Jordan: Timeline — can we start next Tuesday?
[23:55] Maya: Yes. We'll schedule kickoff and connect security.
[24:05] [end of recorded transcript excerpt — call continued with scheduling and follow-up details, light chatter and contact info exchange until 52:00]
[51:30] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and links. Bye.
[51:45] Jordan: Thanks, bye.
next_steps: Send security/compliance pack (SOC2, DPA, KMS docs) to Priya
Share pricing estimate + Optimize cost projection for 1M queries
Provision pilot account and run 10k query benchmark with Curio dataset
Drop SDK and Console quickstart links in CRM note
